components.function: Intercepts user query and identity; resolves user permissions against document metadata tags (e.g., department, security_level) to generate a dynamic filter predicate.
components.name: Permission Checker

components.function: Executes lexical (BM25) and dense (Vector) searches strictly within the subset of documents defined by the Permission Checker.
components.name: Hybrid Retrieval Engine

components.function: Ranks and fuses results from hybrid retrieval using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) or weighted scoring, ensuring diversity and relevance among authorized documents only.
components.name: Score Fusion Module

architecture.subtitle: One concept. Three AI perspectives. One tested architecture.
architecture.title: Permission-Aware Retrieval

trade_off_analysis.rationale: Prioritizes security and compliance over marginal latency gains. Prevents 'prompt injection' via unauthorized data and ensures strict adherence to data governance policies.
trade_off_analysis.rejection_reason: High risk of accidental exposure during retrieval phase; complex cleanup logic; violates 'defense-in-depth' principles.

workflow: 1. Ingest: User query and identity token received.
2. Filter: Permission Checker queries IAM/RBAC service to determine accessible document namespaces/IDs.
3. Retrieve: Hybrid Retrieval Engine executes search constrained by the filter from step 2.
4. Fuse: Score Fusion Module ranks the retrieved authorized documents.
5. Assemble: Final context is passed to the LLM; unauthorized documents are never touched.

changes_made: Refined the architecture description to explicitly define the 'Permission Checker' as a service that generates filter predicates for the retrieval engine.
Clarified the workflow to emphasize that the Hybrid Retrieval Engine operates *strictly* within the filtered subset.

headline: Enhancing Retrieval Systems with Permission-Aware Context Assembly
linkedin_post:
🔒 Security isn't an afterthought in RAG, it's the foundation.

I just shipped a reference implementation for #PermissionAwareRetrieval in our governed enterprise agent stack. By enforcing access controls *before* retrieval (Pre-Retrieval Filtering), we ensure that sensitive data never enters the context window.

✅ Zero unauthorized exposure
✅ Compliance by design
✅ Hybrid retrieval (Lexical + Dense) within safe boundaries

Don't wait for a breach to fix your retrieval pipeline. Build governance in from day one.

#AI #DataPrivacy #RAG #EnterpriseAI #InfoSec #MachineLearning

specification.core_principle: Enforce document access before context assembly (Pre-Retrieval Filtering).
specification.problem_statement: Standard RAG pipelines retrieve documents based on semantic similarity without considering access controls, leading to potential data leakage and compliance violations. The system must enforce access policies before context is assembled for the LLM.
specification.series: From RAG to Governed Enterprise Agents
technical_requirements: Integrate with existing Identity and Access Management (IAM) or Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) systems.
Support hybrid retrieval (Lexical + Dense) within the filtered namespace.
Ensure zero-visibility of unauthorized documents to the embedding model and LLM context window.
Provide audit logs for access attempts and filtering actions.
specification.title: Permission-Aware Retrieval (PAR) Reference Implementation

takeaway: True enterprise-grade RAG requires shifting security left: enforce permissions at the retrieval stage, not the presentation stage. This 'Pre-Retrieval Filtering' architecture guarantees that unauthorized documents are never retrieved, indexed, or exposed to the LLM, providing robust compliance and security.
validation_method: External peer scores only (no self-scoring). Average of two anonymous reviews. Blockers for unsupported claims, fabricated references, critical security flaws. Model agreement alone does not certify correctness.
